Subject: ClearLine redlines: Order Form + a couple of questions on output title

Hi Irene — attaching our redlines to the order form (pdf). Two narrow items we want to confirm before we sign:

1) Output title: We want explicit confirmation that ClearLine retains title to any customer-provided content and to outputs derived solely from that content, but we understand Redwood may use aggregated telemetry and feedback to improve the service. Is that acceptable to you as written in §3.2?

2) Model retrain / product improvements: We are OK with Redwood using non-identifiable telemetry and synthetic feedback, but we need carveouts preventing training on PHI or any customer-provided training datasets unless we opt in. Can you point us to the clause that commits Redwood to the opt-in model?

I've cc'd our counsel Michael for any legal clarifications. We flagged the two paragraphs in the attached PDF.

Thanks,
Claire Jensen
Head of Procurement, ClearLine Health

Subject: Re: ClearLine redlines: Order Form + a couple of questions on output title

Claire — thanks for the redlines and the clear flags. Short answers up front: yes to retaining title to customer-provided content; we can carve out training on PHI and customer datasets to opt-in only. I attached a short response doc that maps our proposed language to each flagged paragraph.

Key points:
- Output title: Redwood proposes language that confirms customers retain title to their input content and to outputs where the output is a verbatim transformation of that content (we define verbatim and give examples). For generative outputs that are novel but heavily derived from provided content, we propose a license-back model (customer retains rights to use, Redwood gets a limited service usage license to serve the account).
- Feedback/training: We will not use any customer-provided data that is marked as "sensitive" or PHI for model training unless the customer executes a separate Training Addendum. For telemetry/feedback (usage signals, prompts and anonymized output quality tags) we propose an aggregated, de-identified telemetry use right.

Next step: suggest a short call between legal teams to agree final redline language. Are you available tomorrow afternoon?

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of GtM Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Draft language and proposed opt-in addendum

Michael / Claire — looping back with proposed clean language (inline below) and a one-page Training Addendum draft. Key selectable options for ClearLine to choose from are marked [OPTION A] and [OPTION B] in the addendum:

- OPTION A (Default service telemetry): Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry (usage metrics, prompt tokens stripped of customer identifiers, model quality tags) to improve and maintain the service. No customer PII/PHI is used.
- OPTION B (Customer training): Redwood may use customer-provided datasets for model training only if the parties execute the Training Addendum and the customer expressly lists the datasets and scope. This adds a separate fee schedule and opt-in steps.

Draft excerpt (for Order Form §3.2):
"Customer retains title to Customer Content and any Outputs that are verbatim or substantially similar to Customer Content. For Outputs that constitute novel generation, Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide license to use Outputs for its business purposes, and Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive license to use Outputs solely to provide and improve the Service in aggregated and de-identified form"

On telemetry retention and deletion: we propose a 365-day default retention for telemetry used to improve models, with the option to shorten retention to 90 days under customer SOC constraints and a process for targeted deletion requests (subject to technical feasibility and audit).

Can we get ClearLine's preferred option and confirmation on retention so we can finalize redlines?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Training_Addendum_Draft_0622.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
